findings.description: The inline policy grants full service-wide control (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) against "Resource": "*" with no conditions, scoping, or permission boundary. Compromise of this single user's credentials yields the ability to read or destroy every S3 object, launch or terminate any EC2 instance, and create/modify Lambda functions account-wide; ec2:* plus lambda:* together also permit privilege escalation via iam:PassRole-adjacent workflows and persistence through attacker-controlled compute.

A static IAM access key is generated for the service user with no pgp_key argument, so the plaintext secret access key is written into the Terraform state file (the encrypted_secret attribute is only populated when pgp_key is supplied). Anyone with read access to the state backend obtains permanent credentials carrying the wildcard policy above; long-lived keys also have no automatic rotation or expiry.

The output "svc_deploy_key_material" publishes the access key's secret material and is not marked sensitive = true, so it is rendered in plan/apply console output, CI logs, and `terraform output`. Combined with the output of the username, this leaks a complete credential pair to anyone able to read pipeline logs.
